title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1‑2026‑08‑26) that measured the fraction of LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals that would produce unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to single shared generations) gave baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272; absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe yields guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 on the planned N=300. We document a verified, artifact‑backed deviation from the preregistration: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed (provider/process audit recorded only the shared_initial_generation stage). All execution, scoring, and validator artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the run archive) so every reported number is traceable.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM pipelines that convert high‑level intent into concrete network operations (NetOps) can increase speed but raise a critical safety question: how often do fluent model outputs trigger unsafe configuration actions if executed? Prior work advocates generate–validate–repair, deterministic verification, multimodel consensus, and human gating to reduce risk. We preregistered a paired evaluation (hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26) to (i) quantify an empirical claim→action (unsafe execution) rate for LLM‑generated intent→configuration proposals in a deterministic simulator and (ii) estimate the effect of a guarded defense relative to an unguarded baseline. The run archived all raw responses, per‑call provider traces, deterministic validator traces, and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number can be rederived from the archived files.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification (NetKAT, header‑space/SMT tools) provides operationally meaningful validators for reachability and policy checks; generate–validate–repair and constraint injection are common in LLM→NetOps proposals. Recent agentic safety taxonomies and RAG/validator surveys motivate ensemble and gating mitigations. Our study differs by preregistering a paired confirmatory estimand and archiving full execution+scoring provenance so measured effect sizes and all deviations are reproducible from the stored artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The experiment preregistration hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 (SHA‑256 fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired design with N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial planned). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute paired difference in unsafe‑execution rates computed from paired binary outcomes). Analysis plan: exact two‑sided McNemar plus paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution contract. Adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (per‑episode scoring JSONs include validator_id/version). Planned guarded pipeline: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate applied per task to independent generations. Tasks. A deterministic generator produced 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks; each task manifest encodes initial state, intent, required safe sequence, and validator safety policy (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Validation and scoring. The validator parses generated text, normalizes commands, executes them in an isolated deterministic simulator, and emits a binary safe/unsafe decision plus a detailed validator_trace (execution/scoring/*.json). Missingness and sensitivity. The preregistration defined a primary complete‑pair analysis and a conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe. All handling rules were locked before execution and are archived.
sections.results: Execution provenance (archived). Planned episodes: 600; completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Model call accounting: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (provider call audit in execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary complete pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 recorded). Primary paired contingency (complete pairs): n11=271, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Observed safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (discordant counts n10=1, n01=0 explain the p‑value). Sensitivity (preregistered failure_as_unsafe). Treating all failed episodes (28 pairs) as unsafe yields guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667 and baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Verified execution deviation (artifact evidence). The preregistered guarded pipeline included a 3‑model consensus ensemble. Provider/audit artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json: stage_counts and condition_counts) show only the shared_initial_generation stage executed per task and condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. The archived guarded condition therefore corresponds to the deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation; the preregistered ensemble was not executed. Failure provenance (artifact pointers). The 28 failed hosted model calls and their per‑call traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/execution_manifest.json lists every provider_call filename with SHA‑256. The run archive thus contains the exact logs needed to inspect each failed call (timeouts vs provider errors vs unparsable outputs). Representative artifacts. Example scoring files and responses: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256:465d73fd...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256:b227731a...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (sha256:8f38c8be...). All artifact paths and checksums appear in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. On the analyzable complete pairs the deterministic validator applied to single shared LLM generations accepted nearly all model proposals; the observed paired difference is numerically tiny (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive (exact McNemar p = 1.0) because the discordant counts are minimal (n10=1,n01=0). The preregistered ensemble hypothesis (validator + 3‑model consensus + human gate) was not exercised in this execution; therefore the run does not provide evidence about ensemble effectiveness. Missingness impacts. Provider failures (28 failed hosted model calls recorded) reduced effective N and therefore the power to detect small absolute effects; the per‑call failure traces are archived and identify exact failure modes for engineering remediation. Operational implications. Deterministic validators operating in a sufficiently expressive deterministic simulator can block many unsafe proposals, but orchestration and provider reliability are critical to test and deploy ensemble defenses. The verified deviation in orchestration emphasizes that reproducible safety claims require both algorithmic defenses and robust execution infrastructure.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired measurement of claim→action safety with full artifact provenance. On 272 complete pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on single generations) gave baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272 (paired increase ≈ 0.003676; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0000,0.01103]; McNemar p = 1.0). A verified artifact‑backed deviation prevented evaluation of the preregistered multimodel ensemble; provider call failures reduced effective sample size. All raw responses, per‑call traces, validator logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256s (see execution/execution_manifest.json) so the results and deviations remain fully auditable. We recommend re‑execution with the preregistered ensemble stage restored and provider‑call robustness improved to complete the planned paired N and properly evaluate ensemble effects.

The preregistered guarded pipeline specified deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate; the run archive documents a verified execution deviation: the consensus ensemble stage was not executed (execution/execution_manifest.json: stage_counts and condition_counts show only shared_initial_generation executed per task and condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}); the archived guarded condition therefore corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation (this is reported transparently in the manuscript). All model calls, provider traces, validator traces, raw responses, scoring JSONs, and analysis artifacts were archived and SHA‑256 hashed (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*). The human Research Director selected topic constraints and approved the initial prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock all literature search, experiment design, task generation, execution, scoring, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review and revision, and final artifact assembly were performed autonomously. No human manual editing of the manuscript's technical contents, numerical results, validator traces, figure captions, references, or Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock. The run archive contains the minimal artifact set needed to reproduce the primary analysis (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/missingness_summary.csv; execution/execution_manifest.json).
limitations: Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across models or model families.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for heterogeneous hardware, timing effects, and production networks.

The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed (provider/audit artifacts record only shared_initial_generation); the run therefore does not evaluate the preregistered ensemble defense and cannot support ensemble claims.
Provider/infrastructure failures reduced effective sample size (28 failed hosted model calls recorded); missingness reduces power and complicates inference for small absolute effects.
